page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-256GB is a general-purpose cloud instance situated within the Cloud Native family, operating under the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 64 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores using an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The CPU subsystem is provided via shared CPU allocation with one thread per core and features 16 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory is configured at 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio.

Hardware resource provisions do not include local storage, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, or dedicated graphics hardware accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, multi-threaded CPU and memory operations perform solidly, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 60,912.88 and strong scores in PassMark CPU extended instructions and encryption routines. Memory caching tests show 4,388.18 GB/sec for small 16 KB read blocks, supporting elevated in-memory transaction performance such as 62.83 million Redis SET operations per second and 425.4 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Single-core execution metrics reflect modest clock rates and shared architecture limits, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10 percent and single-threaded gzip compression registering 22.79 GB/sec. Large uncached memory block throughput averages 142.53 GB/sec for reads and 82.12 GB/sec for writes. Similarly, natural language generation tasks on medium-sized models yield slower output, making the platform less suitable for standalone CPU-based LLM inference. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from high concurrent core density and substantial memory capacity across non-dedicated resources without requiring charges for unneeded bundled disks.

This instance profile is best suited for horizontally parallel workloads that can exploit 64 threads and 256 GB of memory, including distributed caching layers, batch data processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice backends that utilize decoupled network storage.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-256GB is a general-purpose cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor on KVM virtualization. The configuration supplies 64 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz and 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution. No dedicated GPUs or local storage devices are included, requiring external network-attached storage. Benchmarks demonstrate strong parallelized processing and in-memory efficiency, achieving over 60 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier multi-threaded decompression results. However, single-core CPU throughput remains modest due to base clock speeds and shared core scheduling. Delivering high core density and substantial RAM without the overhead of attached physical disks, this server is suitable for multi-threaded batch operations, Redis or Memcached caching tiers, parallel software build systems, and containerized microservices.
